New Name
noo naym
noun
From Revelation 2:17 and Isaiah 62:2; the new name given by God to His redeemed, a token of new and accepted identity.

Biblical Definition

The new name is the new designation God gives to His redeemed, a token of a new, accepted, and intimate identity bestowed by grace. To him that overcometh, the Lord promises, will I give to eat of the hidden manna, and will give him a white stone, and in the stone a new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it. Isaiah foretold it of restored Zion: thou shalt be called by a new name, which the mouth of the LORD shall name; and again, thou shalt no more be termed Forsaken, but thou shalt be called Hephzibah—my delight is in her. Throughout Scripture God marks a new beginning by a new name: Abram became Abraham, Sarai Sarah, Jacob Israel, Simon Peter—the new name signifying a new calling, a new covenant standing, a new character given by God. The new name promised to the overcomer speaks of the believer’s secret and intimate acceptance with God, a name known to him alone in the depths of communion, a token that he is owned, accepted, and beloved. It points to the consummation, when the redeemed shall bear the name of God and of the Lamb in their foreheads, fully His for ever. The dictionary honors the new name as a precious emblem of the believer’s new identity in Christ—owned, renamed, and accepted by sovereign grace—against the false identities the world bestows, and as a pledge of the intimate, everlasting acceptance the redeemed shall know in the presence of their God.

Key Scripture

Rev 2:17 — "He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna, and will give him a white stone, and in the stone a new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it."

Isa 62:2 — "And the Gentiles shall see thy righteousness, and all kings thy glory: and thou shalt be called by a new name, which the mouth of the LORD shall name."

Rev 3:12 — "Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall go no more out: and I will write upon him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God, which is new Jerusalem, which cometh down out of heaven from my God: and I will write upon him my new name."

Isa 62:4 — "Thou shalt no more be termed Forsaken; neither shall thy land any more be termed Desolate: but thou shalt be called Hephzibah, and thy land Beulah: for the LORD delighteth in thee, and thy land shall be married."

Modern Corruption

Identity is sought in self-made or world-given names; Scripture gives the new name by grace, a token of acceptance God Himself bestows on His redeemed.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition beyond the cult of self-made identity. The corruption is the modern quest to name oneself—to forge one’s own identity by self-assertion, or to receive it from the shifting names the world bestows. But the new name of Scripture is given, not seized; it is named by the mouth of the LORD (Isa 62:2), written by God upon His redeemed. True identity is not self-created but grace-given; the soul does not name itself but is named by its Maker and Redeemer.

The principle to recover is that the believer’s new identity is the gift of God, a token of acceptance He Himself bestows. God has ever marked new beginnings by new names—Abram to Abraham, Jacob to Israel, Simon to Peter—each signifying a new calling and covenant standing. To the overcomer He promises a white stone, and a new name written, which no man knoweth but he that receiveth it (Rev 2:17): a name of secret, intimate acceptance, known in the depths of communion with God. He writes upon His own His new name and the name of the city of God (Rev 3:12), and calls the once-forsaken Hephzibah, my delight is in her, for the LORD delighteth in her (Isa 62:4). The new name is the pledge that the redeemed are owned, accepted, and beloved—named by grace, and His for ever.
